name: Hareph
overview: Hareph is a male member of the tribe of Judah, known primarily as the son of Hur. He is identified in Scripture as the founder of Beth-gader, indicating a role in establishing a settlement or community. Beyond this, there are no additional notes or details about his life or character.
namesAndTitles: The name Hareph is a proper name that means 'autumn' or 'sharp; scornful.' This meaning provides insight into the possible cultural or linguistic background of his name, though it was not given by God according to the biblical record.
familyAndRelationships: Hareph is explicitly recorded as the son of Hur. Scripture does not provide further information about his family relationships beyond this paternal connection.
scriptureSignificance: Hareph's significance in the biblical narrative centers on his lineage within the tribe of Judah and his role as a founder of Beth-gader. This highlights his contribution to the territorial and genealogical history of Judah, reflecting the ongoing settlement and development of the land promised to Israel. His mention underscores the importance of familial lines and place-names in the biblical record.
